newsitem.title: UK: British retailers want electricity bills inquiry.
newsitem.headline: British retailers want electricity bills inquiry.

text.p: The British Retail Consortium (BRC) said it would demand an investigation into annual standing charges for electricity imposed by the Pool wholesale market on companies which use over 100 KiloWatts.
In a statement, the BRC said these charges had risen by nearly 300 percent since 1994.

"A significant percentage of the charge contains a substantial levy from money under-recovery...to recoup previous years' losses incurred by the electricity industry as a result of its own mistakes and inefficiencies," BRC director general James May said.
The BRC called on industry watchdog Offer to resolve the matter before liberalisation of the market in 1998.
It said that the amount demanded by the Pool on each meter was "only a small percentage of BRC members' electricity bills."
But it said the charges did not need endorsement from the regulator Offer or explanation of how they were calculated.
"The process by which these charges are levied flouts the principles of transparency and accountability," the BRC said.
